source_title: Civilization #30: Dante as the Second Coming of Homer
summary: This Dante/Virgil lecture is already-public Guide Trap, Love, and Free Will evidence: Dante releases Virgil surgically by making the old guide beloved, exposing his possessive love and false map, then teaching the reader to let him go.

existing_lens_links.episode_phrase: Dante makes Virgil father, guide, narrator, and hero, then the poem shows that Statius can ascend while Virgil would rather remain in hell than admit error.
existing_lens_links.rationale: The public Guide Trap page already uses this source as the surgical-release anchor, and the episode read already links the exact Virgil/Statius/release marks to it.

existing_lens_links.episode_phrase: Desire may arrive naturally, but the person can judge, resist, and curb it.
existing_lens_links.rationale: The public Free Will page already uses this source to name the agency hinge inside love: longing is not an excuse for possession, obedience, or self-deception.

existing_lens_links.episode_phrase: True love wants what is best for the beloved and respects the beloved as priceless rather than turning the person into possession.
existing_lens_links.rationale: The public Love Recognizes The Other page already uses this source as the anti-possession rule before later Tolstoy, Russia, Dante, Homer, and Odyssey layers.

new_lens_seeds.title: Poetic Surgery Rewrites Inherited Memory

new_lens_seeds.title: Doubt As Divine Practice
new_lens_seeds.core_mechanism: Doubt, questioning, debate, and experiment become sacred rather than corrosive when the divine world itself is imagined as open to argument and revision.

chronology_notes.note: Dated 2025-01-14, this source is the earlier public source-trail layer for surgical release before the 2026-04-08 Dante/Virgil guide-trap formulation and the 2026-05-22 Statius lamp layer.
This January 2025 lecture gives an early anti-possession definition: Virgilian love turns the beloved into a controllable fantasy, while Dantean love wants the beloved's good and dignity.

This source predates later public Dante-access and Paradiso formulations with an explicit cognitive model: memorized poetry becomes subconscious building material, so Dante can help produce the Renaissance, Reformation, and Scientific Revolution by changing how readers think below awareness.
